h1: The 6 Best Emerson Smart Alarm Clocks of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Emerson Smart Alarm Clocks: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 Emerson SmartSet alarm clocks scored on wireless charging, Bluetooth version, display brightness controls and wake-up features.
summary: The Emerson CKSW5010 is the best of the lineup: 15W wireless charging, a 3W earbud pad, Bluetooth 5.3 and a dual-alarm FM radio. The 10W Qi model is the value version of the same idea. For a no-frills bedside radio, the CKS1401 adds gradual wake-up volume and a USB-C port, and the plain SmartSet dual alarm remains the cheapest way to get automatic time setting.
intro: Emerson's SmartSet name means the clock sets its own year, month, date and time, and that is the real appeal: no blinking 12:00 after a power cut, no daylight saving fiddling. The catch is that the models differ more in what sits around the clock than in the clock itself. Bluetooth versions range from 4.1 to 5.3, and charging ranges from a basic USB port to a 15W Qi pad.

We reviewed six Emerson clock radios from their published specs, scoring each on wake-up features, charging capability, Bluetooth generation, display readability and backup. Because every unit shares SmartSet and a radio, charging and display brightness carried the most weight, since those are the details you notice every night in a dark bedroom.

products.name: Emerson CKSW5010 Smartset Wireless Charging Clock
products.verdict: 15W wireless charging, an earbud pad and Bluetooth 5.3 in a dual-alarm FM clock.
products.description:
The CKSW5010 has a 15W wireless charger on top, a separate 3W pad for AirPods, a lift-up stand to angle the phone, Bluetooth 5.3 with a range of 10 m and a dual-alarm FM clock.

15W is the fastest charging in the group, versus 10W on the other Qi model, and the lift-up stand keeps notifications visible. It ranks first because it also carries the newest Bluetooth, which is rare on clocks of this type. It costs the most, though.

Buy it if your phone lives on the nightstand. The caveat is that 15W only applies to compatible phones, so older handsets will charge slower.
products.idealFor: People who charge phone and earbuds on the nightstand.
products.skipIf: You only want a simple radio clock.

products.name: Emerson SmartSet Wireless Charging Dual Alarm Clock Radio 10W
products.verdict: A 10W Qi pad, USB port and Bluetooth 5.1 at half the price of the top model.
products.description:
This model offers a 10W Qi charger on top, a USB port rated 2.1A at 5V, Bluetooth 5.1, an aux input and a PLL FM radio. It also sets the time through SmartSet.

It trails the CKSW5010 on charging speed (10W vs 15W) and Bluetooth version (5.1 vs 5.3), but it keeps a wired USB port and an aux input that the top model does not list. That mix makes it the better choice for a household with mixed devices.

It suits couples who share a nightstand. The caveat is the missing earbud pad and the single-band radio.
products.idealFor: Shared nightstands with both Qi and wired devices.
products.skipIf: You need the fastest wireless charging.

products.name: Emerson CKS1401 Smartset AM/FM Dual Alarm Clock Radio
products.verdict: Graduated wake-up volume, a USB-C port and a four-level dimmer in a simple clock radio.
products.description:
The CKS1401 raises volume gradually at wake-up, uses a 0.9 inch white LED with a four-level dimmer, charges through a USB-C port and sets itself with SmartSet. It is an AM/FM dual-alarm radio.

Gradual volume is the feature that matters here, since a sudden alarm starts the day badly. It ranks below the wireless models because it has no Bluetooth or Qi pad, but above the plain SmartSet dual alarm because of the gentler wake and USB-C.

It suits light sleepers. The caveat is the small 0.9 inch display, which is harder to read across a large room than the 1.4 inch panels.
products.idealFor: Light sleepers who dislike abrupt alarms.
products.skipIf: You want to stream audio over Bluetooth.

products.name: Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth Dual Alarm Clock Radio
products.verdict: A large 1.4 inch orange display with auto-dim and Bluetooth 5.1 at a low price.
products.description:
This model has Bluetooth 5.1 audio with a 10 m range, a 1.4 inch orange LED, three brightness levels plus auto-dim, FM radio and a 1.5A USB port at 5V.

The auto-dim is the standout: it lowers the display at night without button pressing. It sits below the CKS1401 only because its USB charging is a slower 1.5A and there is no gradual wake-up, but it adds Bluetooth, which the CKS1401 lacks.

Choose it for streaming a podcast to sleep. The caveat is the 1.5A port, which charges a phone slowly.
products.idealFor: Bedside podcast listeners on a budget.

products.name: Emerson SmartSet Dual Alarm Clock Radio AM/FM
products.verdict: The no-frills SmartSet: automatic time, 20 radio presets and a jade green display.
products.description:
The base model sets year, month, date, day and time automatically, receives AM and FM with 20 presets, shows time on a 0.9 inch jade green LED with a dimmer, and offers a sleep timer, snooze and dual alarms.

It lacks USB, Bluetooth and wireless charging, which is why it ranks fifth. What you get instead is the lowest price and a radio with 20 presets, more than most competitors.

It fits a guest room or a kid's desk. The caveat is that its small display and absent charging port make it a poor fit for a modern nightstand.
products.idealFor: Guest rooms and simple bedside use.
products.skipIf: You want to charge a phone or stream audio.

products.name: Emerson Smartset Alarm Clock Radio with Bluetooth Speaker
products.verdict: A dated Bluetooth 4.1 speaker clock with a 2.1A USB port and a button cell backup.
products.description:
This clock uses Bluetooth 4.1, a 2.1A USB output at 5V, a digital FM radio with 20 presets, a 1.4 inch display and a button cell battery backup.

The backup cell keeps the time through an outage, and the 2.1A port charges faster than the 1.5A port on the newer Bluetooth model. It ranks last because Bluetooth 4.1 is two generations behind 5.1 and pairing can be slower.

It works for a bedroom that needs a USB charger and radio. The caveat is the age of the wireless standard, which limits range and audio stability.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms in areas with occasional power cuts.

whatMatters.detail: Qi pads vary: 10W is moderate and 15W is fast, but only for compatible phones. A dock that charges slowly can leave you short by morning. Check the stated wattage on the listing, and confirm your phone supports it, since many older handsets cap at 5W or 7.5W.

Bluetooth 5.x pairs faster and keeps a steadier connection than 4.1, which matters when you stream a podcast to fall asleep. The listing should state the version and range, such as 10 m. A clock that omits it is likely older, so treat silence as a warning sign.

A bright display in a dark room disrupts sleep, so brightness control is not a luxury. Look for multiple dimming levels, and auto-dim if you can find it. Also check the digit height, since 0.9 inch digits are harder to read than 1.4 inch ones from across a room.

A graduated alarm raises volume slowly, avoiding a jolt that spikes heart rate. A dual alarm lets two people wake at different times. Check the listing for words like graduated or dual, and look for snooze if you tend to doze, but test the buzzer volume yourself.

SmartSet sets the date and time automatically, and a button cell backup keeps the time through a power cut. Without a backup, the alarm may not sound after an outage. If your power is unreliable, look for a backup battery listing before buying.

faq.q: Do these clocks work with every phone for wireless charging?
faq.a: The CKSW5010 (15W) and the 10W SmartSet use Qi, which most recent phones support. A phone in a thick case or an older handset may charge slower than the stated wattage, so remove bulky cases.

faq.q: What mistake do people make buying a clock radio?
faq.a: Assuming every Bluetooth model is current. The Smartset speaker clock uses Bluetooth 4.1, while the CKSW5010 uses 5.3. Check the version, since older standards pair less reliably and drop out sooner.

faq.q: Is the CKSW5010 worth it over the 10W model?
faq.a: If you charge earbuds or want 15W, yes. The CKSW5010 adds a 3W earbud pad and Bluetooth 5.3. The 10W model keeps a USB port and aux input, so it suits shared nightstands better.

faq.q: How do I set up SmartSet?
faq.a: Plug it in and the clock sets the year, month, date, day and time automatically, as on the basic SmartSet and CKS1401. You still set the alarm times, and may need to confirm your time zone.

faq.q: How long does a button cell backup last?
faq.a: The listing for the Smartset speaker clock mentions a button cell but no duration. Replace it yearly as a habit, and keep a spare, because a dead cell loses the alarm during a power cut.

faq.q: Can I use the aux input with a phone?
faq.a: Yes. The 10W SmartSet lists an aux input, so a phone or older player with a 3.5mm cable can play through the speaker. The other models rely on Bluetooth or the radio.

finalTake: The Emerson CKSW5010 earns the top spot by combining 15W charging, an earbud pad and Bluetooth 5.3. The 10W SmartSet is the better value if you want a USB port as well, and the CKS1401 is the pick for gentle wake-ups. Skip the Bluetooth 4.1 speaker clock unless backup matters most.
